ei.subject: ReadingPower유형편완성

fullPassage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks high in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle to fair competition. African farmers earn very low per-hour wages, and they are able to market their tea, cotton, cacao, and bananas at very low prices. But they cannot compete with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. It is up to the rich countries to gradually stop these subsidies — if they really believe their own words about free trade — and to give African farmers their chance.

questions.passage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all (A)[wealthy / poor] countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks (B)[high / low] in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a (C)[serious / minor] obstacle to fair competition. African farmers earn very low per-hour wages, and they are able to market their tea, cotton, cacao, and bananas at very low prices. But they cannot compete with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. It is up to the rich countries to gradually stop these subsidies — if they really believe their own words about free trade — and to give African farmers their chance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) wealthy(부유한), (B) high(높이), (C) serious(심각한) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
✅ ① wealthy — high — serious: 원문 그대로
❌ ② poor — high — serious: poor는 wealthy의 반의어
❌ ③ wealthy — low — serious: low는 high의 반의
❌ ④ wealthy — high — minor: minor는 serious의 반의어

questions.passage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks high in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle to fair competition. African farmers earn very (A)[low / high] per-hour wages, and they are able to market their tea, cotton, cacao, and bananas at very low prices. But they cannot (B)[compete / collaborate] with farmers who (C)[receive / refuse] state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. It is up to the rich countries to gradually stop these subsidies — if they really believe their own words about free trade — and to give African farmers their chance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) low(낮은), (B) compete(경쟁하다), (C) receive(받다) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① high — compete — receive: high는 low의 반의어
✅ ② low — compete — receive: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ low — collaborate — receive: collaborate는 compete의 반의
❌ ④ low — compete — refuse: refuse는 receive의 반의어

questions.passage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks high in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle to fair competition. But they cannot compete with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) gradually(점진적으로), (B) free(자유로운), (C) chance(기회) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① abruptly — free — chance: abruptly는 gradually의 반의
❌ ② gradually — restricted — chance: restricted는 free의 반의어
✅ ③ gradually — free — chance: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ gradually — free — failure: failure는 chance의 반의 뉘앙스

questions.passage: Western ①<u>involvement</u> in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires ②<u>sacrifices</u> from all ④<u>poor</u> countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural ③<u>subsidies</u> ranks high in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle to fair competition. African farmers earn very low per-hour wages, and they are able to market their tea, cotton, cacao, and bananas at very low prices. But they cannot compete with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. It is up to the rich countries to gradually stop these subsidies — if they really believe their own words about free trade — and to give African farmers their chance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ poor(가난한)는 원문 wealthy(부유한)의 반의어 — '모든 부유국의 희생이 필요하다'는 본문 주장과 정반대
det.analysis:
✅ ① involvement: 원문 일치
✅ ② sacrifices: 원문 일치
✅ ③ subsidies: 원문 일치
❌ ④ poor: 원문 wealthy, 희생해야 할 주체는 부유국이지 빈곤국이 아님
det.tip: all wealthy countries(모든 부유국) ↔ poor countries

questions.passage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks high in this category. The majority of Africans today make their living as commercial farmers, and for them, subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle to fair competition. African farmers earn very ①<u>high</u> per-hour wages, and they are able to ②<u>market</u> their tea, cotton, cacao, and bananas at very low prices. But they cannot ③<u>compete</u> with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their ④<u>produce</u>. It is up to the rich countries to gradually stop these subsidies — if they really believe their own words about free trade — and to give African farmers their chance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① high(높은)는 원문 low(낮은)의 반의어 — 아프리카 농부가 '낮은 시간당 임금'을 받는다는 본문 핵심과 정반대
det.analysis:
❌ ① high: 원문 low, 낮은 임금이라는 본문 주장과 정반대
✅ ② market: 원문 일치
✅ ③ compete: 원문 일치
✅ ④ produce: 원문 일치
det.tip: very low per-hour wages(낮은 임금) ↔ high wages

questions.passage: Western involvement in Africa should go far beyond the purchase of oil and minerals, and requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries, Western and non-Western. The matter of agricultural subsidies ranks high in this category. But they cannot compete with farmers who receive state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ abruptly(갑작스럽게)는 원문 gradually(점진적으로)의 반의어 — 보조금을 '점진적으로' 중단해야 한다는 본문 주장과 어긋남
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacle: 원문 일치
✅ ② fair: 원문 일치
❌ ③ abruptly: 원문 gradually, 점진적 중단이 아니라 급격한 중단으로 의미 왜곡
✅ ④ free: 원문 일치
det.tip: gradually stop these subsidies(점진적 중단) ↔ abruptly(급격히)

questions.passage:
(A) African farmers <u>market</u> their tea and cotton at very low prices, relying on traditional trading routes.
(B) Mr. Gupta walked to the <u>market</u> near his house to buy fresh vegetables and bread for dinner.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 market의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) market = 판매하다(내다 팔다), (B) market = 시장(장소)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 시장 — (B) 판매하다: 의미 뒤바뀜
❌ ② (A) 판매하다 — (B) 판매하다: (B)는 walked to the market 장소
✅ ③ (A) 판매하다 — (B) 시장: (A)는 동사 목적어 구조, (B)는 장소
❌ ④ (A) 시장 — (B) 시장: (A)는 동사 쓰임
det.tip: market + 목적어(판매하다) vs. to the market(장소)

questions.stem:

"money paid by a government to help industries or businesses so that they can sell goods at a low price"

det.korean: subsidies(보조금) — 정부가 산업/기업에 지급하여 싼 값에 상품을 팔 수 있도록 돕는 돈
det.analysis:
❌ ① produce: 농산물, 정의와 무관
✅ ② subsidies: money paid by a government to help industries — 원문 state subsidies와 일치
❌ ③ obstacle: 장애물, 정의와 무관
❌ ④ involvement: 개입, 정의와 무관
det.tip: government money to lower prices = subsidies

questions.passage: The majority of Africans today __________ (make) their living as commercial farmers.
questions.stem:

The majority of Africans today (make) their living as commercial farmers.

det.korean: make(동사원형) → make: majority of Africans(복수 취급) + 현재시제
det.analysis: 주어(복수) + 현재시제 → make

questions.passage: But they cannot compete with farmers who __________ (receive) state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce.

But they cannot compete with farmers who (receive) state subsidies to plant, harvest, export, and market their produce.

det.korean: receive(동사원형) → receive: 선행사 farmers(복수) + 관계대명사 who + 현재시제 복수동사
det.analysis: farmers who + 현재시제 복수동사 → receive

det.korean: gradually stop these subsidies(이 보조금을 점진적으로 중단하다) — 부유국의 의무, 자유무역 원칙과 모순되는 보조금을 없애야 한다는 결론

det.korean: subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle(부유국 보조금이 심각한 장애물) — 저임금·저가 수출에도 불구하고 보조금 받는 농민과 경쟁 불가능한 원인
det.analysis:
❌ ① requires sacrifices from all wealthy countries: 빈칸은 아프리카 농민이 겪는 '장애물'의 정체, 부유국 희생의 조건이 아님
❌ ② African farmers earn very low per-hour wages: 저임금은 결과적 사실이지 경쟁 불가의 원인은 보조금
✅ ③ subsidies in rich countries are a serious obstacle: 원문 일치, 장애물의 정체
❌ ④ believe their own words about free trade: 부유국의 약속은 결론부 서술이지 빈칸 핵심 원인 아님
det.tip: subsidies are a serious obstacle to fair competition
